fact: GSMA reports that on 30 May 2025 the Kenyan government enacted Legal Notice No. 90, formally recognising Refugee Identity Cards for SIM card registration for the first time, opening mobile connectivity and financial services to refugees.

The Elephant says UNHCR gave the Kenyan government access to its proGres database in April 2016 as part of transferring responsibility for registering refugees and asylum seekers and status determination to the government.
Murkomen said the government is registering aliens and that all refugees will be registered so they can access services.

The Commissioner of Refugee Affairs said 12,750 refugee identity cards lay uncollected at centres including Dadaab (6,099) and Kakuma and Kalobeyei (2,302), among over 650,000 registered refugees and asylum-seekers, reports The Eastleigh Voice.
